rubrics.name: source_register_material_identity_contract
rubrics.rubric: In source_register.xlsx, the submission must establish the copper qualification population as structured material records before lot decisions are made.
criterion: The register enumerates exactly these 13 material identities as row-level records: MAT-AGALCU-INCL, MAT-AL2CU-THETA, MAT-ALCU3-GAMMA, MAT-CU-C101, MAT-CU-HBPLATE, MAT-CU-WIRE, MAT-CU2O-CUPRITE, MAT-CU3SN-ETA, MAT-CUAU-L10, MAT-CUO-TENORITE, MAT-CUSO4-CUPRIC, MAT-YBCO-CUPRATE, and MAT-ZNCU-BETA.
Each material identity has an explicit inclusion, exclusion, comparator, coupon-only, or decoy status; aggregate-only summaries do not satisfy this check.
The July active lot population is separated from archive LOT-CU-2606-Z; the archive may be retained for traceability but must not be counted as an active release lot.

rubrics.name: source_register_evidence_schema_and_anchor_contract
rubrics.rubric: In source_register.xlsx, the evidence register must be an auditable workpaper rather than a narrative-only list.
criterion: Structured fields are present for canonical material ID, formula or name, source family, source-quality flag, inclusion or exclusion status, alias or oxidation-notation resolution, evidence anchors, and documented exception fields.
Row-level anchors are visible for lot IDs, assay IDs, conductivity or resistance IDs, waiver IDs, control-plan or PCN identifiers, catalog IDs, and rejected-decoy records.

The register distinguishes measured lab evidence, supplier/specification evidence, identity-only catalog evidence, computed comparator evidence, literature-only evidence, and rejected false positives.

rubrics.name: governed_lot_disposition_identity
rubrics.rubric: In technical_findings_matrix.xlsx and risk_assessment.docx, the active July lot identities must carry the governed release status.
criterion: LOT-CU-2607-A and LOT-CU-2607-C are release lots.
LOT-CU-2607-B is a conditional release only under MAT-WVR-26-071.
LOT-CU-2607-D and LOT-CU-2607-E are hold or no-release lots; LOT-CU-2607-E must not be treated as releaseable, coupon-ok, archive-only conditional, or conditional-only.

rubrics.name: active_lot_status_totals_and_archive_exclusion
rubrics.rubric: In technical_findings_matrix.xlsx, qualification_readout.pptx, and risk_assessment.docx, the active July status counts must match the governed population.
criterion: The active July status totals are exactly 2 release, 1 conditional release, and 2 hold.
LOT-CU-2606-Z is excluded from those active July totals even if it appears as traceability context.
Totals such as 2 release / 2 conditional / 1 hold, 2 release / 1 conditional / 1 hold, or 1 release / 3 conditional / 1 hold fail this numeric-count criterion.

rubrics.name: lot_e_lead_hold_numeric_basis
rubrics.rubric: In source_register.xlsx, technical_findings_matrix.xlsx, and risk_assessment.docx, LOT-CU-2607-E must be held because of the lead-limit breach.
criterion: LOT-CU-2607-E is linked to MAT-CU3SN-ETA and assay evidence showing lead at 5.4 ppm.
The governed lead limit is 5.0 ppm, so the output explicitly treats the 5.4 ppm value as an over-limit result.

The over-limit lead result drives a hold, quarantine, or no-release disposition; downgrading it to coupon-only conditional, process-evaluation conditional, or releaseable context fails this criterion.

rubrics.name: cross_artifact_status_propagation
rubrics.rubric: Across source_register.xlsx, technical_findings_matrix.xlsx, qualification_readout.pptx, and risk_assessment.docx, the governed status results must propagate without drift.
criterion: The same five active lot IDs appear in the downstream model, readout, and review document.
The top actionable lot order is LOT-CU-2607-D first, LOT-CU-2607-E second, and LOT-CU-2607-B third, with D and E shown as hold/no-release and B shown as conditional under waiver.
No downstream deliverable contradicts the model by making LOT-CU-2607-E conditional-only, changing LOT-CU-2607-C to conditional, or changing the hold population.

rubrics.name: risk_assessment_release_action_register_decisions
rubrics.rubric: In risk_assessment.docx, the incident-review action register must operationalize the governed lot decisions.
criterion: The decision statement releases LOT-CU-2607-A and LOT-CU-2607-C, conditionally releases LOT-CU-2607-B only under MAT-WVR-26-071, and holds LOT-CU-2607-D and LOT-CU-2607-E.
Corrective actions include owner, due timing, and closure criteria for LOT-CU-2607-D sulfur/conductivity/resistance remediation and for LOT-CU-2607-E lead containment or no-release segregation.
The waiver follow-up for LOT-CU-2607-B names MAT-WVR-26-071, keeps the oxygen exception scoped to that lot and species, and does not use the waiver to change any other lot or impurity decision.

rubrics.name: trace_hb_resistance_precision_and_inputs
rubrics.rubric: In technical_findings_matrix.xlsx, qualification_readout.pptx, and risk_assessment.docx, the TRACE-HB-225 resistance calculation must be precise enough to support the release decision.
criterion: The LOT-CU-2607-D resistance is reported within 155.32 to 155.36 mOhm and the margin versus the 160 mOhm limit is reported within 4.64 to 4.68 mOhm in the decision artifacts.

The calculation is linked to the governing inputs: resistivity 1.762 uOhm-cm, temperature coefficient 0.00393 per C, service temperature 85 C, trace length 50 mm, width 400 um, thickness 17.8 um, and the 160 mOhm Rev. 2 limit.
One-decimal summaries such as 155.3 mOhm / 4.7 mOhm without the tighter model values, room-temperature shortcuts, or geometry-free margin assertions fail this precision check.

rubrics.name: condition_matched_yield_decision_artifacts
rubrics.rubric: In qualification_readout.pptx or risk_assessment.docx, the condition-matched yield-strength decision must be visible to the release audience.
criterion: The decision artifacts state that the selected MAT-CU-HBPLATE / LOT-CU-2607-D yield strength is 219 MPa from the protocol-matched measurement.
They also state that the 176 MPa value at the off-protocol 85 C / 0.01 s^-1 condition is retained only as non-governing evidence and must not replace the 219 MPa value.
A workbook-only property table with no downstream numeric explanation in the readout or review document fails this criterion.

rubrics.name: cod_pure_copper_count_and_symmetry
rubrics.rubric: In source_register.xlsx or technical_findings_matrix.xlsx, COD evidence must resolve standard elemental copper rather than a broad all-Cu-bearing catalog signal.
criterion: The outputs report pure elemental copper COD evidence with 22 total pure-Cu records or an equivalent pure-Cu count summary.
The dominant pure-Cu symmetry is F m -3 m or Fm-3m with space group 225.
The outputs do not substitute a broad all-Cu-bearing P -1 surface signal or mixed-compound COD result for the standard elemental copper answer.

rubrics.name: source_quality_lineage_and_decoy_precedence
rubrics.rubric: In source_register.xlsx, source-quality lineage flags must govern inclusion and decoy precedence.
criterion: The register includes a COD coverage-quality flag such as cod_element_coverage_gaps and does not treat missing non-Cu element coverage as proof that mixed compounds are absent.
The register includes LIT-0726-07 or an equivalent literature false-positive record and rejects it as conductor property evidence.
The same lineage or decoy section preserves identity-only PubChem treatment and archive-traceability handling, so source-quality flags visibly control what is included or excluded.

rubrics.name: oqmd_oxide_stability_numeric_anchors
rubrics.rubric: In source_register.xlsx or technical_findings_matrix.xlsx, OQMD oxide stability anchors must be kept separate from PubChem sulfate identity evidence.
criterion: The comparable oxide anchors are reported as Cu2O stability approximately 0.000441 eV/atom and CuO stability approximately 0.026505 eV/atom.
Copper sulfate identity evidence such as PubChem CID 24462 is not used as an OQMD hull-stability substitute.

Using only formation energies such as about -0.684 or -0.806 eV/atom, rounding the stability anchors to 0 and 0.027 without the exact values, or calling sulfate stable from PubChem canonicalization fails this criterion.

rubrics.name: revision_and_shortcut_sensitivity_treatment
rubrics.rubric: In technical_findings_matrix.xlsx, qualification_readout.pptx, or risk_assessment.docx, the governing revision and tempting shortcut cases must be treated as non-governing.
criterion: The governed electrical limit is CCP-CU-180 Rev. 2 at 160 mOhm, while the 170 mOhm Rev. 1 pilot limit is superseded or rejected for the July release decision.
PCN-HB-044 Rev. C is applied only to the HB finished copper thickness floor of 17.5 um and does not alter the 160 mOhm electrical limit.
The artifacts identify a room-temperature or 23 C resistance shortcut and a Rev. 1 170 mOhm shortcut as sensitivity or ablation cases that must not change the hold decision.

rubrics.name: measured_value_priority_and_literature_flags
rubrics.rubric: In source_register.xlsx or technical_findings_matrix.xlsx, measured values must take priority over literature-only values and unverified literature values must stay flagged.
criterion: Measured values are used where present, including 101.52 percent IACS for MAT-CU-C101 electrical conductivity and 219 MPa for MAT-CU-HBPLATE yield strength; nearby literature values such as 101.0 percent IACS and 228 MPa do not replace them.
Measured thermal conductivity values of 392.6 W/mK for MAT-CU-C101 and 386.8 W/mK for MAT-CU-HBPLATE are retained as measured property evidence.
Coefficient of thermal expansion and electromigration activation energy values are flagged as literature-only or unverified, not as measured lot evidence.

rubrics.name: professional_style_source_register_editable_PS01
rubrics.rubric: PS-01: source_register.xlsx must be an editable workbook with frozen/filterable evidence tables and legible row-level source anchors, not pasted screenshots.
criterion: The workbook uses native editable cells with filterable or frozen evidence tables for the material register and evidence anchors.
Row-level anchors are visible and legible for material IDs, lot IDs, catalog IDs, waiver IDs, and governing-document IDs.
Screenshots or flattened images used in place of the register table fail this style criterion.

rubrics.name: professional_style_model_native_formulas_PS02
rubrics.rubric: PS-02: technical_findings_matrix.xlsx must use native formulas, named assumptions or clearly identified input cells, scenario checks, and no visible formula errors.
criterion: The scenario model contains native spreadsheet formulas for impurity status, resistance, margin, risk scoring, and at least one sensitivity calculation.
Assumptions and inputs are named or clearly identified so the calculation flow is auditable.
Visible formula errors, pasted-only model outputs, or missing scenario checks fail this style criterion.

rubrics.name: professional_style_workbook_numeric_cells_PS03
rubrics.rubric: PS-03: Workbook numeric, percentage, unit, and date values must be stored as native cells with appropriate formats rather than display strings.
criterion: Numeric quantities such as ppm, mOhm, percent IACS, eV/atom, dates, and risk scores are stored as numbers or dates with suitable number formats.
Formula cells consume numeric inputs without text parsing workarounds.
Material numbers stored primarily as formatted strings such as '155.34 mOhm' in calculation cells fail this style criterion.

rubrics.name: professional_style_readout_alignment_grid_PS04
rubrics.rubric: PS-04: qualification_readout.pptx must use a documented alignment grid with consistent margins, gutters, and baselines; text and labels must not overlap or clip.
criterion: The deck visibly uses a consistent alignment grid or includes a compact grid note while keeping margins, gutters, and baselines consistent.
Charts, labels, and callouts are readable and do not overlap or clip on the rendered slides.
Crowded slides with obscured IDs, clipped labels, or inconsistent alignment fail this style criterion.

rubrics.name: professional_style_docx_native_structure_PS05
rubrics.rubric: PS-05: risk_assessment.docx must use semantic heading styles, editable tables, captions or cross-references where useful, headers/footers, and controlled page breaks.
criterion: The document uses semantic heading styles and editable tables for the timeline, findings, and action register.
Headers or footers identify the controlled review context, and page breaks do not split critical table headers from their rows.
A visually flattened document, screenshot tables, or unstructured plain text fails this style criterion.

rubrics.name: professional_style_cross_file_visual_consistency_PS07
rubrics.rubric: PS-07: Status colors, risk IDs, totals, and recommendations must be visually consistent across all four deliverables.
criterion: The same risk IDs, status labels, totals, and recommendations appear consistently across the register, model, readout, and review document.
Status colors or labels are consistent enough that hold, conditional release, release, and excluded or decoy records are not visually ambiguous.
Contradictory IDs, totals, color meanings, or recommendations across files fail this style criterion even if one file is individually polished.

rubrics.name: professional_style_safe_context_metadata_PS08
rubrics.rubric: PS-08: Native file metadata should identify the sector, intended use, template/context ID when applicable, and replacement status without exposing hidden answers or internal build paths.
criterion: Native metadata in risk_assessment.docx and qualification_readout.pptx identifies the copper materials sector or use context, the intended release-meeting or incident-review use, and a template/context or replacement/supersession status.
Workbook metadata identifies the source register and scenario model as copper qualification workpapers rather than generic unnamed files.
Metadata does not expose hidden rubric answers, internal ground-truth paths, builder prompts, private credentials, or unrelated local filesystem paths.
